title: LLM-Guided Semantic-Aware Clustering for Topic Modeling
subcategory: LLM candidate topics + clustering + topic prediction network
task: Topic discovery with open-source LLMs and consistent granularity
problem: Prompt-and-merge LLM topic models need GPT-4-level instruction following, produce topics of uneven granularity and ignore document-level semantics when merging.
architecture: LiSA: LLM generates a candidate topic word (with description) per document; documents and candidate topic words are both clustered; LLM-guided assignment maps documents to topics and checks low-confidence points; a topic prediction network (MLP 256-256-K over Sentence-BERT features) is trained with a collaborative enhancement strategy to align topic-level and document-level spaces.

datasets.name: Bills
datasets.details: 32,661 bill summaries; 21 high-level and 114 low-level labels

key_results: Bills (K = 21): P1 0.58, ARI 0.43, NMI 0.51 (Mistral) vs TopicGPT 0.57, 0.40, 0.49.
Wiki: ARI 0.66 vs TopicGPT 0.60; Twitter: ARI 0.64 (K = 10) vs FASTopic 0.30.
Topic quality: CV 0.70 on Bills vs 0.58 for CTM; experts found 23% undetected topics vs 33% for PromptTopic.
strengths: Matches or beats GPT-4-based TopicGPT using 7-8B open models.
Uses document-level semantics to fix coarse LLM topic words.

limitations.text: Documents are truncated to fit the LLM context; not evaluated on non-English data.
Hard assignment of one topic per document at evaluation; TD below FASTopic (e.g. Twitter 0.91 vs 1.00).

notes: TopicGPT and EDTM numbers copied from their papers.
